reason: The exposed fittings need shelter, so placing fired bricks around the cabin perimeter seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect the bricks to form some kind of protective wall, though I don't know how it will connect to the water line.

alternatives.reason: Wrapping the well line with reflective quilt stock also seems useful, but the stated goal makes the brick shelter my first choice.

reaction: The separate footing makes the shelter’s purpose clearer.
reason: The result points to packing local material against the wall, and the shovel seems suited to that work.
expectation: I expect to pack local material against the wall to help shelter the water-line fittings, though I don't know the exact result.

alternatives.reason: Wrapping the well line could also protect it, but I want to finish the wall preparation first.

effect: The berm shelters the service connections from drifting grit while leaving them accessible and the window clear.
reaction: I like that the covers preserve access to the fittings.

effect: The insulated line now sits in a shallow trench with accessible connections. The covering slows heat loss, but the heat tracing still needs power.
reaction: The distinction between slowing heat loss and supplying heat was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the insulated service trench was most worthwhile because it showed how insulation, powered heat tracing, and access to connections serve different purposes.

leastWorthwhile.text: Insulating the water line was a straightforward intermediate step with little explanation at the time.

surprise.text: I was interested that the wall has its own footing so packed material can rest against it without loading the cabin.

arbitrary.text: The shovel's purpose was initially unclear when it became compatible with the insulated line, although the resulting trench explained it.

continue.text: I would continue: the practical construction details and the reminder that heat tracing still needs power make me curious about what comes next.
